correctness.rationale: For n>=4, adjacent token-pair vertices have degree two, hence domatic <=3, and n=3 gives K3. The modular pair-sum colouring works without edits for 3|n. For other n>=6, exactly four recolourings affect only two wrap-adjacent pairs and closed neighborhoods of the four edited pairs. Explicit lists of eleven/fourteen exceptional states for n>=10/11 and an invariance proof under n->n+3 reduce all lengths to 50 checked local certificate rows. The n=4 K2,4 obstruction and n=5 five-cycle B-colour obstruction prove <=2; connected no-isolate token graphs have domatic >=2. A self-contained standard-library script replays all 50 certificate rows and independently exhausts the 729 and 59049 assignments for n=4 and n=5. Finite tests are not used to infer the infinite proposition.

value.rationale: The exact sharp threshold answers a natural simultaneous-domination (partition) problem on the well-studied two-particle symmetric powers of cycles; two small counterexamples distinguish attainment of the universal minimum-degree bound from failure, and a uniform four-state repair proves attainability for all larger cycles. This is an infinite-family classification with a reusable local-defect method, not a renamed single-set domination bound or an arbitrary fixed-order table.
